clue.text: Express disapproval when Lyttelton entertains a bishop

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the house, so one piece goes inside the name

parts.note: Humphrey Lyttelton, the jazz trumpeter and radio host, was universally known as Humph
taken as written
Right Reverend, the abbreviated title of a bishop

explanation.surface: The broadcaster Humphrey Lyttelton tuts disapprovingly while playing host to a visiting bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyttelton chaired the BBC radio panel game I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue; solvers who know him know the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to clear one's throat gruffly or grumble, a pompous noise of objection.

clue.text: Zany, unending journey in foreign city

indicators.note: something unending has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: zany and mad both mean crazy
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A crazy, never-ending trip abroad around some city overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital of Spain, a city foreign to the British readership of the paper.

clue.text: Chemical drink, containing hint of devilry, transformed doctor

indicators.note: the drink holds the next piece inside itself

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: a mere hint of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of devilry
Dr Jekyll, in Stevenson's story, transforms into Mr Hyde

explanation.surface: A chemical drink, with a touch of devilry in it, turned a doctor into a monster, as in Jekyll and Hyde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' looks like an anagram signal but points to what Stevenson's Dr Jekyll became.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldehyde is an organic compound, such as formaldehyde, so it is a chemical.

clue.text: Magistrate not to think much of terrible disgrace

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not tells us to leave out the words that follow from the magistrate

parts.note: taken as written
to rate someone is to think much of them

explanation.surface: A magistrate who holds someone in low regard over an awful scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to think much of' reads as one phrase meaning despise; split it, so 'not' removes the second part from the official.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or social discredit attached to someone.

clue.text: To be a spiritual healer, a fellow needs quiet to start with

indicators.note: the piece described just before this phrase comes first in the line-up

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
taken as written
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Advice that a man training as a healer must first learn to keep silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal priest or medicine man believed to heal through contact with the spirit world.

clue.text: Son wants meat — not a chunky bit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A boy asks for meat, but only a thin portion rather than a hefty helping.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliver is a thin narrow piece cut off something, the opposite of a thick lump.

clue.text: Jubilant journalist keeps running behind schedule

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the journalist wraps round the next piece

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
something running behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: A delighted reporter is perpetually behind with deadlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means overjoyed or in high spirits, which is what jubilant also describes.

clue.text: Uprooted shelter by sports field

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... of the ground, as two words
second meaning: the covered bench area beside a pitch where players and coaches sit

explanation.surface: A shelter beside the playing field has been torn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants dug out are uprooted; a dugout is the sunken trackside shelter at football and baseball grounds.

clue.text: Father and grotesque friend in panic mode

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, as for a priest
antic is an old adjective meaning grotesque or bizarre
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A priest and his bizarre companion are both in a state of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting frantically means acting wildly and desperately, as someone does when panicking.

clue.text: Glass paper

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Daily ..., a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a material pairing, glass and paper, but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass reflects your image, and the Mirror is a well-known British daily newspaper.

clue.text: Once again get hold of fruit good for plucking

indicators.note: plucking pulls something off, so the letter for good is taken out

parts.note: a greengage is a green variety of plum
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A picker reaches again for a plum that is ripe for picking.
explanation.walkthrough: The first G of GREENGAGE is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reengage is to engage once more, and engage can mean to grip or take hold of, like interlocking gears.

clue.text: Nautical equipment made of hard wood

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
elm is a type of wood

explanation.surface: A piece of ship's gear built from tough timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the tiller or wheel by which a ship is steered.

clue.text: Strange lady embracing another female on French street — very strange lady!

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed next to, so the street follows
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the jumbled word goes round the other woman
strange suggests something made odd, so the letters of the word lady are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
Ann is a woman's name
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: An odd woman hugs another woman in a Parisian street, the scene an odd lady indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Danny La Rue was a famous British female impersonator, a drag artist of stage and television.
explanation.definitionFit: A man performing as a glamorous woman is, playfully speaking, a very strange lady.

clue.text: Irregular act by recipient of VC, one for ever smiling

parts.note: Leonard Cheshire, RAF pilot and charity founder, won the Victoria Cross

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the word act is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual deed by a decorated war hero who never stops grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: The VC is the Victoria Cross, Britain's highest award for gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's Cheshire Cat grins perpetually, its smile lingering even after it vanishes.

clue.text: Sun, one particular paper for troublemaking?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, or Sunday
an edition is one particular issue of a newspaper

explanation.surface: The Sun tabloid and its particular brand of rabble-rousing journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' and 'paper' together suggest the British tabloid, but Sun is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is conduct or speech stirring up rebellion against authority, a serious form of troublemaking.

clue.text: One who saw 13 eating insect in part of Spain

indicators.note: the girl eats the insect, so it ends up inside her name

parts.note: Alice met the grinning cat of 13 across in Wonderland
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A traveller in Spain who spotted a grinning creature swallows a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port city and province on Spain's eastern Costa Blanca.

clue.text: What sounds like open clasp

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the answer is said the same as a word for the next clue word

parts.note: to broach a cask or a subject is to open it

explanation.surface: Something that seems to undo a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is an ornamental clasp or pin fastened onto clothing.

clue.text: Woman prepared meal for old man to eat

indicators.note: the father takes the meal inside, so it sits within his letters

parts.note: your old man is your father, pa

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so the letters of meal are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman cooks dinner for her elderly father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamela is a female first name, so it stands in for an unnamed woman.

clue.text: Drift of stuff that is grey or black, leading to repeated precipitation around break of day

definitions.text: Drift of stuff that is grey

indicators.note: the doubled weather word sits on either side, wrapping the letter from day
leading means going in front, so black comes before the rest

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rain is precipitation

indicators.note: the break of day is dawn, its very beginning, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of day
the same precipitation word a second time

explanation.surface: A weather report: grey or black skies giving way to rain upon rain from dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Grey matter is the brain, so a drift of grey stuff is talent leaving the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain drain is the emigration of skilled and educated people, a gradual drift of intellect abroad.

clue.text: I am given job in tax

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have landed a job at the tax office.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a levy or duty imposed by authority, especially on imported goods.

clue.text: Modern movement born to accommodate someone who's funny

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to house them, so the comic goes inside

parts.note: née, born, introduces a woman's maiden name
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: A modern art trend gives birth to a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age is the late twentieth-century spiritual movement of crystals, alternative healing and astrology.

clue.text: Country artist without measure of intelligence? On the contrary

indicators.note: without here means outside, an old sense of the word
this swaps the roles, so the measure goes outside and the artist goes inside

parts.note: IQ, the intelligence quotient
RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A country whose painter appears to lack brains.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, RA would go outside IQ; 'on the contrary' reverses that, so IQ holds RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a nation in the Middle East, with Baghdad its capital.

clue.text: House with a leak initially allowing in rain a little? One may feel bad staying there

definitions.text: One may feel bad staying there

indicators.note: letting something in places it inside the pieces before it

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of leak is used

parts.note: the first letter of leak
to spit is to rain lightly

explanation.surface: A leaky house letting in a drizzle is no place to stay if you are unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: 'feel bad' means feel ill, not feel guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is where sick patients are admitted and stay while they are treated.

clue.text: Sly person, but with support

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
an easel is a stand that supports a painting

explanation.surface: A crafty character who nevertheless has backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel, figuratively, is a deceitful, untrustworthy person, from the animal's cunning reputation.

clue.text: Old poet — male bastard, one gathered

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: gathered means taken in, so the numeral sits inside the insult

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ancient bard dismissed as a rotter who collected things.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod is mild British slang for an obnoxious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesiod was an early Greek poet, author of Works and Days and the Theogony.

clue.text: A place where silence was demanded by a female writer?

parts.note: taken as written
the Bible says 'Tell it not in Gath', urging silence there about Saul's death
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman author who required quiet wherever she worked.
explanation.walkthrough: Gath was a Philistine city; David's lament in 2 Samuel begins 'Tell it not in Gath'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's name, most famously that of the crime novelist Agatha Christie.
